basis: F-61, G-11: every change from the submitted proposal, with the declared text, v1.0 behaviour, reason and evidence. rows.declared: It is a bidirectional encoder with a typed decision head, which we fine-tune on our own point-in-time labels and calibrate on validation data.
rows.v1_behaviour: No trained decision model ships; H-02/EXP-001 were never run. The scored run trades FS1, a rule-based book (baseline TREND_GUARDED_VOL, policy larp-fs1-final-v1; FS1 = the recovery profile docs/build/evidence/fs1-final-20261025/fs1-final-recovery.json, SHA-256 b8ba06e2..., installed by tools/deploy/prepare_fs1 in live/FINAL mode). Deterministic code sizes, admits and exits every trade. Hosted models only assess SEC filing evidence; a finding counts only after the deterministic verifier matches it to the filing (DEV-19). The trend input is the pinned Binance Web3 token history (IDEA-103). No model output is trained or calibrated.
rows.reason: Training and evaluation data stayed on hold, so H-02 could not be run, and the proposal's own fallback (a pre-registered rule default) applies. The team chose the S1 family on 2026-10-16 (IDEA-075); IDEA-093 froze FS1 on 2026-10-25 from S1 with the IDEA-084 PF-01 values, and IDEA-098 added allowance recovery. EXP-007 was INCONCLUSIVE, so the trend guard ships as declared, not as a proven signal.

rows.declared: P(UP) and the margin P(UP) − P(DOWN) clear thresholds fit on validation data.
rows.v1_behaviour: No probability thresholds. FS1 buys a name only when all of these hold: the PF-04 window (2026-10-29T14:00Z to 2026-11-09T21:00Z) and openState is true (KIT_OPEN_STATE hours, any day); the book is below its target gross by more than the 5% top-up band; target gross = min(trend level, limiter level), with the trend from a five-name equal-weight basket against its 5-session mean (100 bp dead band, start state UP); no 3% daily stop, 8% run stop or 12% deep cut is active; no unresolved red flag; the quote passes 20 bp slippage, the 2 bp impact gate and the 50 bp entry-cost cap on the authorized minimum output plus fee and gas; and the reservation fits cash, the 0.2 USDT cost reserve and the gas budget. At most 3 legs per name per session and 5 attempts per leg. A separate activation self-check may buy one name before trade_after (DEV-24).
rows.reason: No decision model (DEV-01). F-115 made a mostly-cash default unsuitable, so the team adopted the S1 trend-guarded book (IDEA-075) and froze FS1 with the PF-01 values (IDEA-084, IDEA-093). KIT_OPEN_STATE follows the organisers' 24/7 order answer (F-119); the 20 bp slippage follows the measured requote drift (IDEA-093).

rows.declared: Position size = 1% of equity ÷ (2 × expected 5-session volatility).
rows.v1_behaviour: No volatility formula at run time. FS1 holds all five eligible names at fixed equal weights of 1/5 each (frozen in the profile; IDEA-075 inverse-volatility freezing is not used). Target gross is 95% (trend UP, limiter NORMAL), 60% (trend DOWN or limiter CAUTION) or 30% (limiter SEVERE), applied to cash plus marked stock minus the 0.2 USDT cost reserve, with native BNB gas excluded. At 170 USDT that is about 32.3 USDT per name at the high level. Per-trade cap 38.2 USDT, minimum trade 18.64 USDT; a pending level reduction may sell below the minimum only when its quote clears 50 bp and the cost reserve. Positions are not resized on drift inside the band.
rows.reason: With five correlated names and no validated volatility forecast, equal weights need no estimate and fit the caps; the team accepted them in PF-01 (IDEA-084) and IDEA-093 froze them. Gas is excluded from stock capital because F-125 requires a 30 USDT gas swap, which would otherwise starve the fifth name (IDEA-093 PR278-RV01).

rows.declared: ≤ 80% gross exposure, so at least 20% stays in cash.
rows.v1_behaviour: No 20% cash floor. FS1 targets up to 95% gross; the 5% top-up band means buys stop within 5% of the target. Weight cap 30% is the admission limit for any frozen weight (nonbinding at 1/5). The hard trigger is a 35% name weight: above it the name is trimmed back to its operating target. There is no gross trim line, except that the 12% deep drawdown cut trims the book to 40% gross. Drift between target and hard line is held, not traded. BNB gas is outside these weights (DEV-03).
rows.reason: F-115 made a mostly-cash default unsuitable; the team chose S1 at up to 95% gross (IDEA-075) and the PF-01 limits (IDEA-084). A hard line above the target avoids cap-trim micro-trades on small rallies (IDEA-017, IDEA-037).

rows.declared: The order is ≤ 10% of the quoted depth.
rows.v1_behaviour: Price-impact limit: impact ≤ min(50 bp, 2 × logged median) and total entry cost (spread + impact + gas ÷ size) ≤ 50 bp.
rows.reason: The Web3 Open API quote has no depth field; the impact fields replace it.

rows.declared: licensed historical daily prices of the underlying US shares, for training labels. The vendor will be declared at onboarding.
rows.v1_behaviour: No licensed share-price vendor. Sizing and session inputs use the kit's own bStock token candles (Web3 Open API).
rows.reason: Zero paid budget and kit-first data; no trained model needs share-price labels (DEV-01).

rows.declared: a confident DOWN signal on a held name,
rows.v1_behaviour: No DOWN signal. Exits and reductions: (1) a verified 8-K Item 4.02 forces a mandatory SELL of that name (Class 1, DISCRETIONARY_EXIT falsifier authority); verified Items 1.05 and 2.06 (Class 2) block new buys of that name for 5 sessions without a forced sale; only domestic 8-K filers can trigger these, so none can fire for SKHYB (DEV-25). (2) Trend DOWN lowers target gross to 60% and the limiter lowers it to 60% on verified Class 2 findings for two or more names or a multi-name trade restriction, or to 30% on a verified trading suspension, until 3 healthy sessions pass; the excess is sold as pending level reductions. (3) Loss ladder: a 3% daily loss or an 8% drawdown from the peak blocks new buys; the 8% stop clears only below 5% drawdown with a fresh complete reconciled valuation; a 12% drawdown cuts the book to 40% gross and is never cleared. (4) A 35% name weight trims. (5) Terminal flatten from 2026-11-10T19:00Z, signing ends 2026-11-11T14:45Z, flat by 15:00Z. Stale or missing trend data leaves the trend state unchanged; a stale mark never starts a cap trim; a missing valuation blocks new risk. A name may be bought again once its finding is corrected or withdrawn at the source.
rows.reason: No decision model (DEV-01); models only assess evidence (D-11). PF-01/PF-02/PF-05 (IDEA-084) fixed the loss ladder, stop recovery and stale-mark rules, implemented and tested under IDEA-093; IDEA-035 B1 fixed the red-flag classes. Flat at the end so both scoring readings agree (C4).

rows.declared: **Hosted reasoning LLM for the evidence step:**
rows.v1_behaviour: FS1 uses AIandRouting.v4, config/intelligence/aiand-routing.fs1.json (SHA-256 9b86c732...): OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol, medium effort, is the primary assessor; AIand moonshotai/kimi-k3 and zai-org/glm-5.3, both high effort, are independent reviewers and fallback. An ASSESSED primary stands unless a reviewer dissents or abstains; without one, a reviewer result is used by fixed precedence, or the assessment is UNAVAILABLE. Every claim is deterministically verified against the filing before it counts. Models never size, sign or place orders. Without the OpenAI key every assessment goes to the AIand reviewers. OpenAI spend is paced over a frozen US$50 budget.
rows.reason: The unsigned v3 trial was retired (IDEA-066); IDEA-083 parallel review and IDEA-093 per-stage output limits form v4. The model-adoption decision for the scored run is recorded in IDEA-093 MA-01 and passed to prepare_fs1 as --model-adoption-ref. Hosted-provider rights are recorded in MODEL_PROVIDER_RIGHTS_20261018.md; live rate limits under five parallel workers were not measured.

rows.declared: an event-calendar planner,
rows.v1_behaviour: Omitted: no per-class macro/earnings event-calendar planner ships. In the existing S1 limiter the SCHEDULED_EVENT evidence class alone cannot cut exposure; IDEA-075 O5 stays a separate decision. The frozen session/execution windows, the terminal schedule and every market, terminal and execution-window safety gate stay in force; they are not presented as a planner.
rows.reason: Decided 2026-10-19 by Keegan, accepting the PC-OPS01 recommendation: a planner needs a trusted event source with provenance, per-class action/freshness/window rules, conflict precedence, replay/audit fields and tests, which cannot be built and qualified before the Oct 22 decision cut. Finalised in the GAP-62 review (IDEA-042 GAP62-F01, 2026-10-21).

rows.declared: A gas-reserve floor keeps enough gas for exits.
rows.v1_behaviour: Initial gas only (LD07, 2026-10-20): v1 plans no gas top-up rounds. The only BNB is the F-120 first-gas swap: pre-first-agent-trade MetaMask USDT to BNB seeding, gas paid in USDT, recorded as a funding note rather than an ai-seeds round and sized for the whole run. The floor is kept by refusing new buys that would cut into the exit gas reserve; reductions and exits continue. If gas is exhausted the agent cannot trade, so the reserve and the seeding size must cover the full final exit. The reserve is sized at the signer's cap gas price and minimum-trade sizing at an expected gas price (LD09-B, 2026-10-21); exact reserve and seeding values are pinned in the selected profile.
rows.reason: Funding is USDT only and gas is BNB only; the proposal did not say how the floor is refilled. Native top-up routes cannot be decoded or proven in time (#30), so Keegan chose initial-gas-only operation on 2026-10-20 (IDEA-061 LD07).

rows.declared: The loop is capped at 6 calls and 60 s per decision.
rows.v1_behaviour: Each evidence assessment has at most 6 tool calls and 180 s. The OpenAI primary gets at most 60 s (one third of the decision budget) and up to 3 of the tool calls; if review is needed, the two AIand reviewers run concurrently with at most 90 s each and split the remaining tool calls. Output caps: OpenAI 4,096 tokens, each reviewer 16,000. Stage prompts are hash-pinned (primary.md, review.v2.md). Up to 5 issuers are assessed in parallel and up to 4 continuation rounds may follow a slot. A late reply never restores authority; worker cleanup is tracked separately from stage deadlines.
rows.reason: IDEA-083: high-effort review exceeded the 60 s serial budget even with an assessed primary, so the budget was lengthened and review parallelised. IDEA-093 PL added parallel issuers and continuation rounds. Adopted with the assessor (DEV-19, IDEA-093 MA-01).

rows.declared: The order aborts if quoted slippage exceeds its cap.
rows.v1_behaviour: The kit router (a diamond proxy) and its swap facet publish no verified source, so on-chain enforcement of the minimum output, recipient and deadline is unproven, and the wallet address is not in the swap calldata. FS1 runs in untrusted-router mode (policy 05759e90...): it refuses any quote whose minimum is below the 20 bp cap or that uses an RFQ maker, checks the full calldata layout, and before every swap step re-checks on chain the pinned facet and code and that the router allowance is at most this swap's amount. Allowance recovery is enabled (IDEA-098): after an aborted swap, and before the next stock intent, the executor sends zero-amount approve revokes, at most 8 children per action (up to 5 other-token revokes, the approve, and the swap or a pay-token revoke), within the original authority and the CAP-02 gas ceilings (1.2M gas at 0.16 gwei; 0.001536 BNB per action, 0.01536 BNB exit reserve). The revoke takes the spender and gas from the API (approveAmount "1") and signs only amount 0 (IDEA-104 OBS03-B1). The signer policy allows only these steps. A fill below its minimum is never booked and stops all further signing.
rows.reason: Keegan chose the untrusted-router direction (IDEA-070); Isaac accepted API-provided router behaviour (B09-TRUST01). Run 4 showed that a leftover allowance could block the flatten (IDEA-096), so FS1 enables recovery (IDEA-098). Exact approvals, signer caps and settlement checks limit submitted authority and detect anomalies, but cannot prove that the router honours recipient, minimum output or deadline, set a maximum loss, or recover a bad fill. The zero revoke had not been confirmed on chain when this was written (B1-5).

rows.declared: full pipeline for 5+ days including a weekend, at minimum size

Rehearsal was shadow operation plus short signed runs on the development wallet, 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-27: runs 4 and 5 built and mostly sold a book (IDEA-089, IDEA-097; run 4's flatten was blocked by a leftover allowance, IDEA-096); runs 7 and 8 made no or aborted entries (IDEA-104 OBS01, OBS03); the S5-COST03 run completed one BUY. On the final wallet, F-125's self-check is a separate temporary run (IDEA-110): one 0.90 USDT SKHYB BUY, then a full SELL, on 2026-10-28 before the F-127 pause; its outcome is recorded in IDEA-110. FS1's own built-in self-check window (to 2026-10-28T23:00Z) ends before FS1 plans its first round, so it is journaled EXPIRED and makes no trade.
rows.reason: Gate B was not passed by 2026-10-21, so D-DN-02 applied: shadow plus a shorter signed window (Keegan, 2026-10-17). Defects found in the signed runs were fixed (IDEA-096/098, IDEA-104 OBS03-B1, FENCE01/02). F-127 paused projects at 2026-10-28T10:00Z, after the planned FS1 install time, so the final-wallet check ran as IDEA-110.

rows.declared: **SEC EDGAR:** 8-K, 10-Q and 10-K filings, time-stamped by their acceptance time.
rows.v1_behaviour: The red-flag exits (Class 1 CRITICAL, Item 4.02 restatement; Class 2 SERIOUS, Items 1.05 cybersecurity and 2.06 impairment) are read from domestic issuers' own Form 8-K and 8-K/A filings only (`red_flags.v1.json`, `filer_classes: ["DOMESTIC"]`). SK hynix, behind SKHYB, is a foreign private issuer with no 8-K item codes, so none of these exits can fire for SKHYB; its events stay ordinary evidence and the Class 3 WATCH statements stay SHADOW for every name. SKHYB stays in the five-name universe. No 8-K authority is inferred from foreign-filer text and no SHADOW statement is promoted.
rows.reason: The team chose to keep all five names, accepting SKHYB's asymmetric adverse-event coverage and common technology exposure as opportunity/coverage risk rather than build unqualified foreign-filer predicates or drop the name (IDEA-084 PF-03, the decision for #39). This is a coverage-risk acceptance, not a claim of equal protection or of outperformance.
